units.function: Provides Paperclip's broad operator/Agent CLI surface for access and identity, Companies and portability, Agents, Goals/Projects/Issues/Runs, approvals, costs, feedback/evidence export, plugins, Skills/Team catalogs, Secrets, Routines, execution workspaces/environments and local context/token enrollment. The 28 files are mostly thin API wrappers plus substantial client-side portability, export, archive, credential and supply-chain workflows.
units.dependencyDirection: Commander command modules -> shared schemas/types and CLI common/context/http clients -> Paperclip server REST endpoints. Several paths bypass the common transport with raw fetch for assets, attachments, plugin streams and org images; plugin scaffolding imports a repository-internal source package; zip.ts is only a compatibility re-export from @paperclipai/shared/portability-zip. Product policy, presentation, local filesystem, credential selection and remote mutation are mixed in the command layer rather than separated by stable application ports.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Agent, Goal, Project, Issue/comment/document/work-product/attachment/interaction/tree-hold, Approval, HeartbeatRun/event/workspace operation, Routine/trigger, Environment/lease/workspace, Plugin/tool/job/bridge/config/local-folder, CompanySecret/provider/access event, Skill catalog/audit/update/runtime snapshot, Team catalog/import preview, cost/finance/budget event, feedback trace/bundle and local profile/token. Human identity is usually collapsed to board, system or optional user metadata; operational ownership is frequently Agent-only.
units.lifecycle: Resolve API origin/profile/persona/Company/Run and bearer credential -> validate selected inputs with a mixture of shared schemas, ad hoc parsers or raw JSON -> call REST endpoints -> render JSON/text/files or launch follow-up actions. Multi-step workflows such as Company import, Agent prompt+wake, token enrollment, Skill bulk update, Team approval fallback and inline-Secret migration are non-transactional client orchestrations without one durable request digest, idempotency contract or rollback. Destructive and high-risk commands use inconsistent confirmation, and several preview/apply flows are not cryptographically or revision-bound.
units.testAssessment: All 28 implementation files were read exactly once at the pinned SHA and relevant per-file history was recorded in the oversized-unit ledger. CLI TypeScript checking passes. Existing focused Company CLI tests were reused without rereading: delete 9/9, export-force 5/5, import URL 11/11, ZIP 1/1 and main Company 18/18 passed; import/export E2E remained skipped after embedded PostgreSQL startup failed. Related server/schema/test units remain independently auditable and no command-layer result is treated as proof of server authorization, transactionality, archive safety, plugin isolation or Secret redaction.
units.designRationale: The CLI maximizes API parity and supports local/self-hosted operations without requiring the Web UI. Valuable choices include typed shared validation in selected domains, explicit Company context, sequence/byte cursors, environment capability and lease views, Secret usage/access events, catalog hashes, non-executing Skill audit, desired-vs-runtime reconciliation, source default-deny flags, installed-origin drift, Team/Company preview and destructive confirmations in selected paths. Compatibility re-exports and headless projections reduce client duplication when narrowly applied.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs an independent automation/operator interface for managed and self-hosted deployments, but every executable action must preserve accountable-human responsibility, tenant/data authority, Connector neutrality, approval pause/resume, evidence/result lineage and safe credential/export behavior. It also needs versioned FDE templates, Skill/Connector supply-chain governance, environment leases and operational recovery without inheriting Paperclip types or runtime.
units.companyOsFit: Use Paperclip as a design and failure-mode reference only. Current best-reference candidates are the Skill catalog/hash/audit/hold/pinned-origin/desired-runtime model and the Team catalog's content-hash, installed-missing and external-source default-deny ideas. Independently implement stable Company OS commands/events over Identity, Organization, Connector, Data, Approval, Evidence, Secret, Environment and Asset/Renderer ports. Require structured error codes, bounded streaming, safe paths, audience-bound short-lived credentials, preview/apply digests, idempotency, revision checks and durable sagas/outboxes.
units.responsibilityConflict: Board authentication is not a verified accountable human; Agent credentials can create/self-assign work and request broad mutations; Goals/Projects/Teams lead through Agents without mandatory human owners. Approval links and fallback requests are not exact action/revision/permission/data/evidence digests and often require an unbound rerun. Credentials, Secrets and sensitive payloads can appear in argv/output; ambient context can select the wrong tenant; exports and runtime commands lack data-owner approval and complete chain-of-custody records.
evidence: research/paperclip/in-progress-read-ledger.json application:cli/commands/client: 28 pinned files, 13,148 lines, exact completed ranges, SHA-256 inventory, per-file history and findings

Focused Company CLI test evidence reused without source reread: delete 9/9, export-force 5/5, import URL 11/11, ZIP 1/1, main 18/18; import/export E2E skipped after embedded PostgreSQL startup failure
units.securityFindings: Critical patterns include configurable API-origin plus configurable credential-env-name exfiltration; plaintext keys/Secrets/prompts in argv or output; unaudited long-lived tokens; raw terminal-controlled server/plugin/Agent text; arbitrary-path and symlink-unsafe exports/downloads; bundle path traversal in feedback export; unbounded file/archive/network/log buffering; telemetry of repository URLs/local paths; non-atomic Secret migration; unbound preview/apply and approval reruns; plugin/Skill/Team supply-chain installation without complete capability/data/Secret admission; direct runtime commands without exact approval; English-string authorization/error control; and inconsistent idempotency, revision, pagination and rollback. Positive controls are noted but are not sufficient Company OS boundaries.
